purpose: Startup source inventory of the 44 commands outside the selected 35-command O1-O13 set; no implementation or acceptance promotion
interpretation: Paths and one-based line ranges resolve at source_revision under source_root. Every row includes actual source plus declarations; declarations alone do not establish support.

Options list accepted parser spellings or expression grammar observed in source, including recognized rejection paths where identified. They are not a completed alias/conflict/repeat/error-precedence contract.
Common standalone metadata is --help and --version; exact invocation behavior remains command-specific. Catalog contract() appends these metadata entries at core/cli/catalog.mbt:1-27.

Generic cli.parse supports --, short clusters, attached values and long=value but keeps scanning options after operands; individual commands may normalize first or use independent parsers. Catalog names may be semantic identifiers, not literal accepted long aliases.
Current support labels are inherited declarations, not fresh GNU/POSIX, Native/Wasm, platform, published-consumer or performance verification.
Documented API boundaries are conditional current project policy, not fresh absence proofs of released dependency APIs. Algorithm work must not be relabeled as an API gap.
All rows still need applicable frozen-oracle option/operand/conflict/error-prefix/effect cases at their owning implementation stage. No oracle conflict was resolved by this inventory.

base32.operands: Zero or one FILE; omitted/- is stdin; wrap defaults to 76 and zero disables wrapping.
base32.observed: Encoding/decoding, wrapping, garbage policy and padding validation already exist; input is read_all before transformation.
boundaries: C-byte stream profile; invalid-data prefix/error behavior and full padding/alias conflicts remain unverified here
Whole-input buffering is source-visible; no streaming or performance acceptance follows

base64.operands: Zero or one FILE; omitted/- is stdin; wrap defaults to 76, zero disables wrapping.
base64.observed: Existing byte encoder/decoder with strict padding, optional ignored garbage and width validation; input is buffered.
boundaries: Full oracle invalid-data/prefix/order behavior not rechecked
Whole-input processing is not an incremental codec claim

basename.operands: NAME [SUFFIX] by default; -a or -s enables NAME...; -s implies multiple.
basename.observed: Lexical path/suffix handling, multiple operands and NUL separators exist.
boundaries: Declared C-byte/portable lexical profile; host path and locale edge parity unverified

cat.operands: FILE...; omitted/- is stdin. Numbering state spans operands.
cat.observed: Byte copy and selected formatting modes already exist; -u is accepted as a documented no-op.
boundaries: C-byte display profile; locale display/signal/closed-output parity not promoted

chmod.operands: MODE FILE...; numeric mode or closed symbolic assignments such as a=rwx/u=rw,g=r,o=.
chmod.observed: Numeric modes and restricted complete symbolic assignments exist; recursion and verbose output exist. Reference mode rejects before mutation.
boundaries: Windows permission mutation is rejected by platform policy
Reference/incremental/copied/omitted-class/X/s/t modes need permission-read semantics; restricted symbolic assignments exclude directory/link cases
Command-line numeric symlinks and recursively encountered symlinks have distinct handling
declaration_findings: Some API diagnostic/documentation text still names async 0.22.4 while workspace dependency is 0.22.5; this is stale version wording, not proof that the gap has been lifted

column.operands: FILE... or stdin; inputs are combined before layout. Width comes from option, COLUMNS or 80; zero/unlimited modes have dedicated behavior.
column.observed: Grid/table layout and separator controls exist; non-ASCII input bytes use escaped display in the declared C profile.
boundaries: Non-ASCII separators reject
Auto terminal width/full Unicode width/full util-linux grammar are outside the current profile
Current layout materialization is not the required R2 same-snapshot spool implementation

cp.operands: SOURCE... DEST, at least two operands. Prefix normalization handles optional update/backup and preserve forms.
cp.observed: New-file/tree copies with explicit --no-preserve=mode and selected no-clobber/update no-ops exist; traversal and backup/overwrite decisions are implemented.
boundaries: Default mode preservation rejects without public permission reads
Existing regular-file overwrite rejects without identity/handle truncation; -f does not lift that gate
Symbolic sources require supported follow policy; no symbolic-link-copy implementation or metadata-preserving fallback

curl.operands: URL...; credentials need explicit user:password rather than an interactive password prompt.
curl.observed: Substantial HTTP transfer, Basic authentication, cookies, redirect/upload/retry/timeout/output modes exist. Preserve calibrated stage-0 framing/prefix/file/error-priority profiles.
boundaries: HTTP/1 profile, no complete curl protocol/config/HTTP2/auth/PSL/IDNA parity
Content coding is retained as wire bytes; no automatic decompression/compressed option
Path-based retry reset cannot guarantee descriptor/inode identity after replacement
Repeated ordinary request-header semantics remain project work, not a list API gap
declaration_findings: --noproxy is implemented at options.mbt:269 and documented in help:90 but absent from catalog:230-237

date.operands: At most one +FORMAT. -d accepts selected ISO civil input or @SECONDS with up to nine fraction digits; TZ/TZDIR select timezone.
date.observed: Current time, explicit input, C-profile format fields, 64-bit TZif/POSIX future rules and ISO/email formatting exist; internal normalized option is named iso.
boundaries: Relative/free-form GNU date grammar, clock setting and unsupported modifiers reject
Ambiguous/gap local civil times reject; local database absence needs TZ or -u
Current host-clock precision and exact formatting conflicts remain unverified

diff.operands: Exactly FILE1 FILE2; - is stdin. Unified and context modes conflict; context count is bounded.
diff.observed: File-only normal/unified/context/brief/binary/identical rendering already exists. Inputs are materialized; Myers reconstruction stores a copied frontier map per edit distance at compare.mbt:42.
boundaries: Current algorithm is not the planned O(N+M) auxiliary-space D implementation
Selected whitespace/case/blank-line/recursive/new-file modes are project work; current help explicitly excludes them
Ambiguous edit ties/hunks are not certified to GNU ordering; timestamp/TZ and no-final-LF contracts need preserved evidence

dirname.observed: Lexical dirname with ordered multiple outputs and NUL mode exists.
boundaries: Portable lexical/C-byte profile; platform separator and root edge parity unverified

echo.operands: STRING...; parsing stops at first unrecognized cluster/operand. -- is a literal operand.
echo.observed: Newline suppression and selected C-byte escape expansion exist; metadata has special standalone handling.
boundaries: No universal generic-parser semantics; POSIXLY_CORRECT/locale modes not claimed
Catalog enable-escapes/disable-escapes/no-newline are semantic IDs, not accepted long aliases

expr.operands: EXPRESSION token argv; one initial -- is removed; metadata recognized standalone.
expr.observed: Precedence-aware integer/string expression evaluation and shared regex adapter already exist.
boundaries: C-byte strings; pattern backreferences/word assertions and locale collation are excluded
Matcher expansion is S1 project work; no host regex fallback or new public-API blocker established

false.observed: Normal exit is 1; standalone metadata exits 0.
boundaries: No GNU startup/performance acceptance was measured

find.operands: PATH... precedes expression; default path is .; -- escapes the next path in the path-prefix loop. Batched -exec + has expression-placement and action-count restrictions.
find.observed: Traversal, boolean expression tree, selected metadata/access predicates and ordered actions already exist; avoid replacing these as missing functionality.
boundaries: No general -H/-L link traversal/full GNU expression grammar/owner/link-target/birth-time claims
Selected special-file/time combinations and action-error precedence need actual backend/oracle evidence
Catalog is an expression-summary contract, not a complete lexer table

fold.observed: Incremental byte/C-profile display columns, tabs/backspaces and space folding exist; invalid input bytes are retained.
boundaries: Full Unicode/locale display width is not claimed; long-record and partial-error behavior still require execution

grep.operands: PATTERN [FILE...] when no -e/-f; otherwise FILE...; - is stdin. Multiple -e/-f patterns exist.
grep.observed: Literal/BRE/ERE modes, C-byte leftmost-longest adapter, matching/output/context/recursive/file-selection behavior exist.
boundaries: Backreferences, word assertions and unsupported engine syntax reject; full locale/worst-case matcher performance remains project work
-r/-R share the recursive parser identity; distinct symlink traversal parity was not established
declaration_findings: README:23-24 attributes pattern backreferences to a public regex-engine limit; code explicitly rejects them in the project adapter, and the new plan assigns a pure MoonBit matcher to S1. Do not perpetuate this as an established public-API blocker

gunzip.operands: FILE... or stdin; named decompression requires -c unless testing; root delegates to core/gzipops.run.
gunzip.observed: RFC1951 stored/fixed/dynamic decoding, concatenated members, CRC/ISIZE and delivered-prefix errors exist; compressed input is entirely buffered.
boundaries: Reader-based incremental input decoding is G2 project work, not an API blocker
Named replacement/metadata restoration remain an independent documented filesystem boundary

gzip.operands: FILE... or stdin; named encoding requires -c -n; named decompression requires -c unless testing.
gzip.observed: Workspace encoder calls released async 0.22.5 Encoder.write_reader/end with bounded LZ matching and fixed Huffman. Shared decoder also exists. This source inventory did not inspect or execute the active published encoder; historical README version text does not establish its encoding behavior.
boundaries: Levels -1..-9/--fast/--best, 32KiB history, dynamic compression/cost selection and Reader decoding remain project work
Current candidate support records 1KiB history/64-byte max match; performance/ratio have not been measured here
Metadata-aware named replacement is separate from compression algorithms

head.operands: FILE... or stdin; count parser supports selected signed 64-bit counts and suffixes; last lines/bytes selects mode.
head.observed: First/negative-tail line or byte selection, NUL records and headers exist.
boundaries: Negative counts retain required suffix state; source support is not a memory-scaling acceptance
Unlisted aliases, pipe-read boundaries and error-order parity remain unverified

jq.operands: FILTER [FILE...] with current default-identity/from-file paths; - is stdin; argument preparation packs two-value variable options.
jq.observed: moonjq0.2.0 evaluation with a public-AST Unicode-scalar slice adapter and current input/output/variable modes exists; main_native filename does not limit the package to Native.
boundaries: No complete jq module/streaming/language parity; moonjq adapter/profile limits are documented
Logs conflicts with null/raw input are explicit rejections; auto terminal color is not claimed

jqlog.operands: QUERY plus optional inline INPUT; - or absent input reads stdin; file input uses -f. Manual parser accepts the separate --file PATH form.
jqlog.observed: JSONL/log record framing, malformed-line skipping, selected log format and shared jq-filter evaluation exist on declared Native/Wasm targets.
boundaries: No full jq language/streaming guarantee; --file=PATH is not registered by this manual parser
Malformed/prefix/large-log behavior needs execution, not filename-based inference

ln.operands: TARGET... LINK or -t DIRECTORY TARGET...; -t and -T conflict.
ln.observed: Symbolic-link creation with relative/target/overwrite/backup decisions exists; requesting default hard links rejects before mutation.
boundaries: Public hard-link API unavailable in documented policy; Windows symbolic creation is conservatively rejected
Follow/no-follow/backup/race and prompt-channel oracle parity not rechecked

make.operands: VARIABLE=VALUE and TARGET...; manual option grammar. -C is a separate-argument form, not evidence of literal --directory support.
make.observed: Existing parser, dependency graph, recipe execution and bounded parallel ready-queue scheduling are substantial prerequisites; -j is implemented.
boundaries: No GNU jobserver, full implicit-rule/secondary-expansion/make language guarantee
Export handling excludes bare export/unexport; catalog directory is a semantic identifier
Shell/child execution inherits current explicit process boundaries

mv.operands: SOURCE... DEST, at least two operands; normalized optional update/backup forms.
mv.observed: Files/directories and selected links, overwrite/no-clobber/update/backup/recovery paths exist. Keep stage-0 Windows Native link rename behavior and conservative Wasm gate.
boundaries: Equal-time interactive/update targets require identity; no-clobber remains a successful skip
EXDEV means rename failed; metadata-preserving cross-device copy fallback is unavailable and is not silently performed
Windows Wasm link/junction rename remains rejected pending verified host behavior

nl.operands: FILE... or stdin; numbering/sections continue through the command stream.
nl.observed: Selected a/t/n numbering styles, logical-page sections, width/start/increment/format and blanks grouping exist.
boundaries: pBRE style and complete locale grammar are excluded; actual large numeric/record limits not newly executed

paste.operands: FILE... or stdin; repeated - operands consume successive records from shared stdin.
paste.observed: Parallel/serial paste, delimiter cycling and selected escaped/NUL delimiters exist; delimiter validation precedes input.
boundaries: C-byte profile; repeated stdin, EOF padding and later-open/read errors need preserved oracle contracts

patch.operands: [ORIGINALFILE [PATCHFILE]]; -i and positional patch input cannot duplicate; explicit target/output cannot ambiguously bind a multifile patch.
patch.observed: Unified/context parsing, reverse, zero-fuzz exact application, dry-run/stdout, safe target-name stripping and /dev/null creation/deletion paths exist. Existing-file writeback rejects in preflight.
boundaries: Nonzero fuzz, offsets and .rej output are project work, separate from file identity/metadata writeback boundaries
Named --output rejects; current safe existing-path refusal must not be removed by parser expansion
Current hunk mismatch abandons that file and continues later files; D-stage partial-hunk/.rej semantics remain to implement and freeze

printenv.operands: Optional NAME...; absent names print all environment entries.
printenv.observed: Ordered selected-name values and newline/NUL output exist; missing names set status1 while retaining other values.
boundaries: Host environment enumeration and ordering are current profile, not full locale/environment parity

pwd.operands: Extra non-option operands are ignored with a diagnostic; last L/P determines mode; POSIXLY_CORRECT affects default.
pwd.observed: Logical PWD validation and physical current directory paths exist; validation compares normalized realpaths.
boundaries: No independent inode-identity proof; current working-directory and realpath backend behavior remains relevant

rmdir.observed: Directory removal and parent traversal/verbose/selected ignored-failure behavior exist.
boundaries: Parent removal has partial effects; full permission/path/diagnostic oracle parity not certified

sed.operands: SCRIPT [FILE...] unless ordered -e/-f scripts are supplied; FILE... share numbering/state. Compilation precedes input.
sed.observed: Existing p/d/q/=, s with g/positive occurrence/p, replacement captures, positive/$/regex/range/! addresses and ordered scripts are reusable.
boundaries: Hold space, labels/branches, groups, multiline commands and append/insert/change remain S project work
Pattern backreferences/word assertions and matcher scaling need pure MoonBit project implementation; replacement captures already exist
In-place editing is a separate documented identity/metadata boundary and is not registered by the current parser
declaration_findings: Catalog:355 lists in-place although -i/--in-place is absent from the parser and help/support explicitly exclude editing
Catalog extended-regexp is a semantic spelling different from accepted --regexp-extended/--extended; do not treat catalog names as aliases

sh.operands: FILE ARGS..., -c SOURCE NAME ARGS..., or stdin; explicit -i uses the current pipe/session interaction.
sh.observed: Existing lexer/parser/expansion, functions/control flow, child execution and incremental Session interface are substantial current features.
boundaries: Session/REPL is not a full PTY or job-control terminal
Arithmetic/fd duplication/backticks/background jobs and exec/fg/bg/jobs/wait are outside the declared language profile
This plan does not add #31 language/PTY scope

sleep.operands: One or more nonnegative fractional DURATION operands with s/m/h/d suffix; sums seconds.
sleep.observed: Fractional/summed duration handling exists; milliseconds round upward then clamp to 2147483647.
boundaries: Source-visible cap silently shortens requests above approximately24.86days; no long real-time wait was performed
Signal/clock scheduling behavior and overflow/Infinity grammar remain unverified oracle questions
declaration_findings: README/help/support do not disclose the source cap; comment says never waits less than requested while the clamp necessarily can

test.operands: EXPRESSION tokens; no expression exits1; malformed/trailing expressions exit2; no generic option parser.
test.observed: Current string/integer/file-kind/access/size/time predicates and logical expression parser exist.
boundaries: No implemented isatty -t, same-file -ef or full owner/mode predicate suite
Special-file positive cases, timestamp races and legacy ambiguous operand grammar need exact backend/oracle evidence

timeout.operands: DURATION COMMAND [ARG...]; other option-looking tokens reject. Duration uses bounded millisecond conversion.
timeout.observed: Local direct-child timeout execution exists with124 timeout and125/126/127 error classes.
boundaries: Local-only; not among78published commands
No process-group/tree termination guarantee, signal selection, kill-after or full GNU job-control semantics
Direct-child hard cancel cannot establish cleanup of daemon-owned resources

touch.operands: FILE...; missing paths may be exclusively created with default permissions; -c on a missing path is a no-op.
touch.observed: Missing-file creation/no-create behavior exists; existing paths and explicit timestamp selectors reject before attempting unsupported setters; earlier created outputs survive later failure.
boundaries: Public timestamp setter capability remains the documented unlock; parsing alone does not implement timestamp behavior
declaration_findings: Existing-path diagnostic still names async0.22.4 although current workspace is0.22.5; fresh public-API discovery is required before lifting the boundary

tr.operands: SET1 [SET2] with mode-specific arity; C-byte sets/classes/escapes/equivalence/repeats.
tr.observed: Current translation/deletion/squeeze/complement paths and set grammar exist.
boundaries: Full multibyte/locale collation semantics are excluded; conflict/expansion/invalid-set oracle matrix still required
No startup/performance acceptance was measured

unlink.observed: Single-path no-follow unlink and directory refusal exist.
boundaries: Full permission/special-file/backend error-wording parity not revalidated

wget.operands: URL... plus optional input-file URLs; selected explicit HTTP methods only.
wget.observed: Existing HTTP transfer, Basic/cookie/retry/resume/output/log modes are substantial; preserve stage-0 partial-body/Range/selected-name/zero-body and retry wire behavior.
boundaries: No FTP/recursive/HSTS/full progress/IDNA/PSL/full GNU Wget parity
Timestamping and metadata behavior retain documented capability limits
--idle-timeout is an explicit project extension, not proof of a GNU alias
Repeated ordinary headers remain project semantics work

which.operands: NAME...; direct paths or PATH search; Windows PATHEXT and empty/duplicate PATH entries have source paths.
which.observed: Regular executable lookup and all/silent modes exist; no shell alias/function introspection.
boundaries: Provider/version/profile must be frozen before differential claims; a host which binary is not a substitute
Platform executable/read/access semantics need actual backend evidence

yes.operands: STRING... joined with spaces; default y; other option-looking operands remain text.
yes.observed: Repeated line output exists; current main catches all stdout write errors and exits successfully.
boundaries: Accepted closed-pipe profile is not proof of signal parity or equivalence for every output error
Sustained throughput and cancellation were not measured here

zcat.operands: FILE... or stdin; implicit decompression to stdout; root delegates to shared gzip runner.
zcat.observed: Same current RFC1951/member/checksum/prefix decoder as gunzip; compressed input is read_all.
boundaries: Reader input is G2 project work
Suffix search/force pass-through/metadata restoration outside current profile
